# Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection via Fake Crack/Mod Site

**Exercise date:** 2024-11-26 (traffic starts 04:49:38 UTC)
**Evidence:** `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap`, `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt`

## Victim host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.11.26.183 |
| MAC | d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (FQDN `desktop-b8tqk49.nemotodes.health`) |
| AD domain | NEMOTODES.HEALTH (DC: NEMOTODES-DC, 10.11.26.3, MAC 00:24:e8:7f:09:5d) |
| Logged-in user | `oboomwald` |

Grounded in: ARP (IP↔MAC), NBNS/mDNS (`DESKTOP-B8TQK49`), and Kerberos AS/TGS exchanges (`kerberos.CNameString=oboomwald`, service names `host/desktop-b8tqk49.nemotodes.health`, `krbtgt/NEMOTODES.HEALTH`).

## Malware family

**NetSupport RAT** (commodity RAT abusing the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-access protocol). **Signature-confirmed**, not just behavioral:

- Suricata alerts fired directly on the traffic: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin/Response`, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`.
- Confirmed independently by following the TCP stream to 194.180.191.64:443: cleartext HTTP (not TLS) with `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` and `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.8 (Windows NT)`, exchanging `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD` beacons to `POST /fakeurl.htm` roughly every 60 seconds for the rest of the capture (68 POSTs, from t=67s to t=3231s).

## Infection chain (as observed in traffic)

1. `10.11.26.183` resolves and browses **classicgrand.com** (→ 213.246.109.5) at t≈33s — the referring/lure site.
2. Immediately after, resolves and browses **modandcrackedapk.com** (→ 193.42.38.139) at t≈36s, flagged by Suricata as `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup / TLS SNI (modandcrackedapk.com)` — a fake cracked-software/mod-APK download portal, the likely delivery vector. This session runs entirely over TLS, so the dropped payload itself was not recoverable from the capture (encrypted, no plaintext object to export or hash).
3. At t≈67s the host begins polling **194.180.191.64:443** with the NetSupport RAT protocol — infection is live.
4. At t≈67s it also queries `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (→ 104.26.1.231) and performs a `GET /location/loca.asp`, a NetSupport RAT geolocation check-in against legitimate NetSupport infrastructure abused by the RAT.
5. Beaconing to the C2 continues for the remainder of the capture (~54 minutes) at a steady ~60-second interval.

No transferred file could be captured or hashed — every relevant delivery/C2 leg after the initial DNS lookups is either TLS-encrypted (classicgrand.com, modandcrackedapk.com) or a small text-based POST/response with no attached binary object (`fakeurl.htm` bodies are the `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD` beacon text itself, 22–306 bytes, not a file).

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint (confirmed C2 checkin):**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — NetSupport RAT C2 server (plaintext HTTP masquerading on port 443)

**Malicious/lure domains:**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` → 193.42.38.139 — fake crack/mod download site (ZPHP), likely infection vector
- `classicgrand.com` → 213.246.109.5 — preceding referrer/lure site in the same browsing session

**Abused legitimate infrastructure (RAT feature, not attacker-owned):**
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` → 104.26.1.231 (also 104.26.0.231, 172.67.68.212) — NetSupport geolocation lookup, `GET /location/loca.asp`

**Malicious URL:**
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` — RAT C2 beacon endpoint (POST, `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD`)

**Files/hashes:** None recoverable. No plaintext file transfer was present in the capture; all payload-carrying sessions were TLS-encrypted.

**Context, not IOCs (benign, ruled out):** all Microsoft/Bing/MSN/Office/Windows Update/telemetry domains, Google/gstatic/Adobe/createsend.com traffic — normal enterprise workstation background noise. The `ETPRO [MS-EFSR]`, SMBv1, and NTLMSSP alerts at 04:49–04:50 are workstation↔DC (10.11.26.3) traffic only, consistent with routine AD/SMB activity on this host, not attributed to the RAT infection.
